jobs.title: Field Technician
jobs.description:
Are you ready to build a career where every day brings new challenges, hands\-on learning, and meaningful environmental work? Provost \& Pritchard is seeking a motivated **Field Technician** to join our Environmental team.

  



You will spend most of your time in the field collecting samples, supporting drilling and well installations, and collaborating with engineers, scientists, contractors, and clients. You will also build technical skills through data analysis, reporting, mapping, and project coordination.

  



If you enjoy working outdoors, solving problems, learning by doing, and contributing to work that matters, we’d like to hear from you.

  


**What You’ll Do:**


* Collect soil, soil vapor, indoor air, groundwater, surface water, and other environmental samples.
* Conduct aquifer and pump testing, drilling oversight, and soil logging in support of monitoring well projects, including monitoring well installation, development, purging, and sampling.
* Maintain clear, accurate field notes, sampling logs, forms, and project documentation.
* Coordinate with drillers, surveyors, equipment operators, laboratories, landowners, regulatory agencies, subcontractors, and clients.
* Assist with environmental investigations at contaminated or hazardous sites, including inspections, data collection, and technical support.
* Organize data for reports, spreadsheets, databases, maps, graphs, and cross sections.
* Support permitting and regulatory compliance activities, including work involving California Well Standards and agencies such as Regional Water Quality Control Board (RWQCB) and Department of Toxic Substances Control (DTSC).
* Help coordinate subconsultants, requests for proposals, schedules, and field activities.
* Contribute to projects that meet established scopes, schedules, budgets, quality standards, and safety requirements.

  


**Qualifications:**


* A high school diploma or GED is required; an Associate or Bachelor’s degree in geology, engineering, environmental science, or a related field is preferred.
* Interest in environmental investigation, remediation, and field\-based work.
* Strong written and verbal communication skills.
* The ability to prepare accurate field documentation and technical records.
* Working knowledge of Microsoft Excel and comfort learning databases and other technical software.
* A detail\-oriented, dependable approach and the ability to work both independently and as part of a team.
* Sound judgment, professionalism, and a commitment to safety.

  


**Certifications:**


* OSHA 40\-Hour HAZWOPER certification is preferred but not required.

  


**What to Expect**



This is an active, hands\-on position with approximately **70% fieldwork and 30% office\-based support**. You will work outdoors in changing weather conditions and may travel or work early mornings, evenings, weekends, or extended hours depending on project needs.

  

Candidates must be able to lift and move up to 50 pounds and perform field activities that may involve standing, walking, stooping, kneeling, crouching, crawling, working near water, and wearing Level D personal protective equipment.

jobs.title: Hiring Now! Assistant Project Coordinator
jobs.description:
### **Description**

  

Arellano Associates (AA) is a professional community outreach firm specializing in the transportation, clean energy, and water sectors. We bridge the gap between government agencies and the public by combining meaningful, digital and in\-person engagement with innovative technology to deliver a transparent and accessible communication process for our client's projects.  

  

By creating engagement opportunities for stakeholders to have a genuine voice in the planning and decision\-making process, we build trust, encourage collaboration, and help reduce disparities; working together toward a more connected, sustainable, and equitable California.  

  

The Assistant Project Coordinator (APC) is a full\-time, entry\-level role on the front lines of that work, supporting public outreach and stakeholder engagement for a project team under the guidance of a Project Manager. The position calls for learning agility, the ability to pick up new tools, including AI, quickly and apply them well. It also calls for ownership and follow\-through, the discipline to get the details right on a public meeting, a mailer, or a project update, since those are the details that ultimately make an impact on the communities we serve. This position is also a launchpad into a career in public outreach and project delivery, with plenty of room to grow within the company.  

  

Check out some of the Projects we are working on and how we are making an impact to communities all throughout Southern California!: https://www.arellanoassociates.com/projects  

### **Key Responsibilities**

  

* **Content Creation:** Draft written text for collateral materials including fact sheets, brochures, newsletters, posters, e\-communications, and social media content.
* **Messaging Support:** Help tailor draft content to project goals and different audiences, building an understanding of how messaging shifts depending on the community and client you're working with.
* **Event Coordination:** Support in\-person public engagement events such as public meetings, pop\-ups, and special events, including logistics, supplies, and staffing.
* **Public Interaction:** Engage directly with community members at outreach events, facilitate participation, and help gather public feedback that shapes project strategy.
* **Tech Tools \& AI:** Apply the latest tech tools, including AI tools such as ChatGPT, Copilot, and Claude, to communicate project information and gather public input, using platforms like ArcGIS, SurveyMonkey, MetroQuest, Poll Everywhere, Typeform, Google Forms, Constant Contact, Salesforce, SharePoint, and WordPress.
* **Creative Production:** Use Adobe Creative Suite programs, including InDesign, Illustrator, Photoshop, and Premiere Pro, for basic file creation and editing.
* **Vendor Coordination:** Coordinate vendor services including printing, catering, translation and interpretation, and toll\-free phone lines.
* **Database \& Website Management:** Keep stakeholder databases, project websites, and social media content current and accurate.
* **Digital Engagement:** Monitor public input coming through email, project websites, helplines, and online engagement tools, and flag issues or notable responses to your project manager promptly.
* **Task Tracking:** Organize and maintain project documentation, support scheduling, and help the team track progress and coordinate resources.
* **Project Support:** Complete tasks within timeframes and budget parameters, helping ensure timely and cost\-effective delivery.
* **Issue Communication:** Communicate issues and challenges to your project manager promptly.

  

### **What We Look For:**

 **In Every Team Member*** **Learning Agility:** You take feedback well and treat the unfamiliar as something to figure out rather than avoid. This industry and role will be new to most people who take it on, so you're the kind of person who asks a clarifying question instead of guessing. You are comfortable asking questions, jumping into something new, and curious about new technologies.
* **Ownership and Follow\-Through:** You follow through on what you say you will do, whether that's a deadline on a fact sheet or a task from a morning check\-in. When something's off, whether it's a typo you caught or a vendor that fell through, you speak up early instead of hoping it resolves itself, and you take pride in getting the details right.
* **Collaboration and Mentoring:** You work well with others and know a project runs better when everyone's pulling in the same direction. You help teammates succeed, whether that's covering an event when someone's out or walking a newer team member through a process you've already learned. Ultimately, you make the people around you better at their jobs.
* **Curiosity with Technology and AI:** You're comfortable picking up new software and tools, including AI tools like ChatGPT, Copilot, or Claude, and applying them to real tasks. Whether that's drafting a first pass at a newsletter or researching a project topic, you know good AI use means checking the work, not just accepting it.
* **Professionalism:** You represent yourself, AA, and our clients well in every interaction. From a public meeting to an internal email. You ask questions rather than guess, show up on time and prepared, and handle mistakes with maturity.

**For This Role*** **Public Interaction:** You're comfortable talking with members of the public, whether that's staffing a table at a community event, answering questions at a public meeting, or fielding a call from a concerned resident. You can translate technical project details into plain language, and you stay professional even when someone's frustrated. No professional outreach experience required, we'll help you build it.
* **Writing and Content:** You can put together a clear, accurate first draft, whether it's a fact sheet, a newsletter article, a social media post, or a project update. You take direction well on tone,

As we foster a culture of inclusion throughout our company and within our communities, we constantly ask ourselves: What is our impact on the world?


We believe electricity powers modern life. As part of our Power sector, you’ll help shape how electricity is generated, transmitted and delivered as global energy demands grow. From massive data centers to modernizing transmission systems, our industry\-recognized engineers and scientists have been at the forefront of grid transformation for more than a century. You’ll work side\-by\-side with these experts and contribute to reliable, resilient and sustainable power systems, helping communities thrive and industries expand. This isn’t just a job, it’s a chance to drive infrastructure forward, power innovation and leave your mark on our energy future.

HDR is looking for an **Environmental Scientist 1** to support utility clients with environmental and construction permitting and compliance. * Accommodating changing project schedules and scopes – shifting attention as needed.
* Managing tasks between competing project interests; tracking workload with support of supervisor.
* Effectively communicate over phone, email, or messaging platforms.
* Review local, State, and Federal regulations for applicability to projects
* Perform pre\-construction and post\-construction site visits
* Review engineering design packages for environmental / local permitting compliance
* Develop permitting matrices and timelines – for integration into client templates or overall schedules


The candidate would work with an experienced team including other environmental scientists and project managers of varying experience and backgrounds. Candidate responsibilities would evolve to include:

* Coordinating directly with client and permitting approval agencies representing HDR
* Directing internal resources/supporting staff (CAD/GIS, wildlife biologists, land agents, public outreach)
	+ Coordinating/attending field visits
	+ Overseeing deliverable production
	+ Review deliverables for consistency with client project scope
* Managing deliverable production and distribution
	+ Upload and track permitting submittals through jurisdictional permitting portals
	+ Conduct file management per client and internal specifications
* Development of figures and map sets in coordination with GIS/CAD staff

**Preferred Qualifications**

* Minimum 2 years of experience.

* Strong technical writing skills, including experience preparing technical reports, agency correspondence, permit applications, and other project documentation.
* Experience on active construction sites.
* Strong organizational skills and ability to work in an environment with changing deadlines and priorities.
* Ability to understand hydrology across disturbed landscape, read topographic maps, and visualize erosion and sediment transport.
* Self\-motivated, able to work independently and as part of a team.
* Ability to safely drive around the State either in personal car or Company rental is a must. A valid Colorado driver’s license is required.


Our team understands the value of expanding individual work portfolios and experience to keep job duties interesting and achieve career sustainability and growth. Additional workload and type would depend on skills, experience, and interest. A comfort and enthusiasm interacting with a variety of individuals will help foster successful career growth.


Team members are currently working from Fort Collins, Denver, and remote locations along the front range and western slope of Colorado. The preferred candidate will be based out of the Fort Collins office. Flexibility on number of days in the office and working remotely is expected, with the assumption that the candidate would be in office 2\-3 days per week to facilitate training and skill development. Long\-term remote vs in office time is negotiable and will be based on past experience and level of training required. Our team encourages a healthy work\-life balance that focuses on quality of service to our clients and participation in recurrent meetings while allowing for flexibility in work schedules. Site visits are sporadic with limited/few visits during winter months and up to 2\-3 visits per month during busier months. Site visits rarely require overnight stay.

  

While this posting is for a full\-time (40\-hour per week) position, a part\-time (minimum 30\-hours per week) is also an option.

**Environmental Scientist 1**


 \- (195554\)
At HDR, our employee\-owners are fully engaged in creating a welcoming environment where each of us is valued and respected, a place where everyone is empowered to bring their authentic selves and novel ideas to work every day. As we foster a culture of inclusion throughout our company and within our communities, we constantly ask ourselves: What is our impact on the world?


We believe electricity powers modern life. As part of our Power sector, you’ll help shape how electricity is generated, transmitted and delivered as global energy demands grow. From massive data centers to modernizing transmission systems, our industry\-recognized engineers and scientists have been at the forefront of grid transformation for more than a century. You’ll work side\-by\-side with these experts and contribute to reliable, resilient and sustainable power systems, helping communities thrive and industries expand. This isn’t just a job, it’s a chance to drive infrastructure forward, power innovation and leave your mark on our energy future.  

  

Watch Our Story:' https://www.hdrinc.com/our\-story'  

  

Each and every role throughout our organization makes a difference in our ability to change the world for the better. Read further to learn how you could help make great things possible not only in your community, but around the world.  

  

HDR is looking for an **Environmental Scientist 1** to support utility clients with environmental and construction permitting and compliance. This role has a primary focus on construction stormwater management permitting and compliance, with supplemental work supporting floodplain development permitting, wetland permitting, right\-of\-way permitting, local planning approvals, and wildlife compliance support.

**In this role, the candidate would be expected to:**

* Supporting ongoing project compliance through construction (reviewing inspection reports, attending routine calls, post\-construction site visits and documentation).
* Accommodating changing project schedules and scopes – shifting attention as needed.
* Managing tasks between competing project interests; tracking workload with support of supervisor.
* Effectively communicate over phone, email, or messaging platforms.
* Review local, State, and Federal regulations for applicability to projects
* Perform pre\-construction and post\-construction site visits
* Review engineering design packages for environmental / local permitting compliance
* Develop permitting matrices and timelines – for integration into client templates or overall schedules


The candidate would work with an experienced team including other environmental scientists and project managers of varying experience and backgrounds. Candidate responsibilities would evolve to include:

* Coordinating directly with client and permitting approval agencies representing HDR
* Directing internal resources/supporting staff (CAD/GIS, wildlife biologists, land agents, public outreach)
	+ Coordinating/attending field visits
	+ Overseeing deliverable production
	+ Review deliverables for consistency with client project scope
* Managing deliverable production and distribution
	+ Upload and track permitting submittals through jurisdictional permitting portals
	+ Conduct file management per client and internal specifications
* Development of figures and map sets in coordination with GIS/CAD staff

**Preferred Qualifications**

* Minimum 2 years of experience.
* Experience in Bluebeam, GIS or CAD drafting.
* Experience in local or federal permitting or agency review processes.
* Strong technical writing skills, including experience preparing technical reports, agency correspondence, permit applications, and other project documentation.
* Experience on active construction sites.
* Strong organizational skills and ability to work in an environment with changing deadlines and priorities.
* Ability to understand hydrology across disturbed landscape, read topographic maps, and visualize erosion and sediment transport.
* Self\-motivated, able to work independently and as part of a team.
* Ability to safely drive around the State either in personal car or Company rental is a must. A valid Colorado driver’s license is required.


Our team understands the value of expanding individual work portfolios and experience to keep job duties interesting and achieve career sustainability and growth. Additional workload and type would depend on skills, experience, and interest. A comfort and enthusiasm interacting with a variety of individuals will help foster successful career growth.


Team members are currently working from Fort Collins, Denver, and remote locations along the front range and western slope of Colorado. The preferred candidate will be based out of the Fort Collins office. Flexibility on number of days in the office and working remotely is expected, with the assumption that the candidate would be in office 2\-3 days per week to facilitate training and skill development. Long\-term remote vs in office time is negotiable and will be based on past experience and level of training required. Our team encourages a healthy work\-life balance that focuses on quality of service to our clients and participation in recurrent meetings while allowing for flexibility in work schedules. Site visits are sporadic with limited/few visits during winter months and up to 2\-3 visits per month during busier months. Site visits rarely require overnight stay.

  

While this posting is for a full\-time (40\-hour per week) position, a part\-time (minimum 30\-hours per week) is also an option.

**Required Qualifications**  

* Bachelor's degree in Environmental Sciences or closely related field
* Knowledge of wetland delineation, field investigation techniques, and agency coordination requirements
* Excellent writing and communication skills
* MS Office experience
An attitude and commitment to being an active participant of our employee\-owned
